The two 10 MW reference wind turbines studied are the INNWIND.EU/DTU and AVATAR turbines.
The INNWIND.EU/DTU turbine has a rotor diameter of 178.3 m and a rotor speed of 9.6 RPM.
The AVATAR turbine has a rotor diameter of 205.8 m and a rotor speed of 9.6 RPM.
The CFD computations are performed for an isolated rotor only, neglecting the effect of tower and nacelle, and under uniform axial flow (no wind shear) conditions.
The computational grid has a total size of 14 million cells, with 256 cells around the airfoils, 129 cells in the span-wise direction for each blade, and 129 cells in the wall normal direction.
The y+ values at the surface are kept below 1 everywhere on the blade surface.
The pressure/velocity coupling is enforced through the SIMPLE algorithm, and the QUICK scheme is used for the differencing of the convective terms in the momentum equations.
The k-ω SST turbulence model and the Drela/Giles version of the En transition model are used in the CFD computations.
The results show good agreement between the evaluated methods at the mid-span (0.30 < r/R < 0.85) of the blades.
Deviations are observed at the root (r/R < 0.30) and tip (r/R > 0.85) regions of the blades, attributed to the 3D effects of the bound circulation.
The inverse BEM method uses empirical relations to correct for the breakdown of the simple momentum theory at high axial induction factors (a > 0.4).
The Shen 1 method is more sensitive to the monitoring point location near the root compared to the Shen 2 method.
The Ferreira-Micallef and Herra´ez methods do not show dependency on input parameters such as monitoring point location.
The AAT method is limited to capturing the mean value of the axial induction factor over one rotation and cannot capture the dynamics of the induced velocity in yawed flows.
The 3-Point method is able to reproduce the dynamic behavior of the induction and AoA near the tip and root of the blade.
